title: What If the Moon Disappeared? (And 3 More What Ifs)
next: Tomorrow: 4 space mysteries nobody can solve!
description:
What if the Moon just... disappeared? What if Earth stopped spinning, or the Sun switched off? The Cosmozibs crew answers 4 wild space questions!

{{chapters}}

A new episode every day. Join the crew: https://www.youtube.com/@Cosmozibs?sub_confirmation=1

Voices in this video are AI-generated. Every fact is checked with the sources below.

#space #spacefacts #sciencefacts

lines.say: Hey, space cadets! Today we ask the wildest questions in the universe!
What if the Moon disappeared? What if Earth stopped spinning?
What if the Sun switched off? And what if you drove a car all the way to the Sun?
What if we skipped the questions and went straight to snacks?
Here's the plan. Four big questions, four wild answers, and a quiz after each one.
I love quizzes! I'm going to win every single one!
Nice try, Rocky. Stay until the end, every story has a quiz! Tick tock, let's go!
What if, one night, the Moon just... vanished?
Wait... WHAT? No more Moon?! How could this happen?!
Don't worry, it won't really happen. But let's imagine it!
First, the oceans would change. The Moon's gravity drives Earth's tides!
The Sun pulls on the oceans too, but with a little less than half the Moon's tide power. So the tides would get much smaller.
Smaller waves? The surfers are going to be sad!
Hmph. Finally, a beach day without the water chasing me.
Bonus fact! Some birds use moonlight to help them travel at night.
And on the Great Barrier Reef, corals time their spawning with the rising Moon!
There's an even bigger problem. Right now, Earth's axis is tilted about twenty three degrees, and it only wobbles a little.
Without the Moon, scientists think that wobble could get wild. Our seasons could stop being predictable!
Summer in the morning, winter by lunch? That's crazy!
And without moonlight, nights would be darker. Only the stars would light up the sky.
Good news: the real Moon isn't going anywhere. You can wave at it tonight!
I waved at it once. It didn't wave back.
So tonight, go outside with a grown-up and look for the Moon. Can you spot it?
Quiz time! What drives most of Earth's tides? The Sun, the Moon, or the wind?

show.q: What drives most of Earth's tides?

lines.say: The Moon! Its gravity pulls the oceans into bulges, and that makes high tides.
Next question: what if Earth stopped spinning?
What if our planet slowly stopped spinning?
Stop?! But I'm still dizzy from the last spin!
Right now, Earth spins once every twenty three point nine hours. That's why we have day and night.
If it stopped, one day would last half a year. And the night would last half a year too!
Six months of night? That's the longest bedtime ever!
Imagine having only one sunrise every year!
I'd set my alarm clock for next year!
The day side would get super hot, the night side super cold, and strong winds would rush between them.
Great. A planet with a bad hair day for six months.
Bonus fact! Earth's spinning helps turn the molten iron inside it into a giant magnet.
That magnetic shield protects us from radiation from space. Some birds even use it to find their way!
So the spinning Earth is like a big protective bubble? Cool!
Exactly! Spinning keeps us safe, and it gives us a sunrise and a sunset every single day.
And here's a real fact. Earth's day is getting longer, very, very slowly.
About one second longer every fifty thousand years. So don't wait up!
Quiz time! How long does Earth take to spin once? About twelve hours, twenty four hours, or one week?

show.q: How long is one Earth spin?

lines.say: About twenty four hours! To be exact, twenty three point nine.
Next... what if someone switched off the Sun?

short.title: What If the Sun Switched Off?

lines.say: What if the Sun switched off, right now?
Everything goes dark instantly, right?
Nope! We would still see the Sun shining for about eight minutes and twenty seconds!
Wait... WHAT? How could this happen?!
Because sunlight needs time to travel. The Sun is about one hundred and fifty million kilometers away!
The light that hits your face right now left the Sun about eight minutes ago!
So the Sun is basically always late. Just like me.
Bonus fact! Light is the fastest thing there is. It zooms at about one billion kilometers per hour!
Even at that speed, the trip from the Sun to us still takes eight minutes. That's how far away it is!
So when I look at the Sun... wait, should I look at the Sun?
Never look straight at the Sun! It can hurt your eyes. Scientists always use special protection.
Sunlight also gives plants the energy to grow. That's where lots of our food comes from!
Without the Sun, Earth would slowly get colder and colder. So let's keep it switched on!
I promise I'll never complain about sunburn again!
Quiz time! How long does sunlight take to reach Earth? Eight seconds, eight minutes, or eight hours?

show.q: How long does sunlight take to reach us?

lines.say: About eight minutes! Eight minutes and twenty seconds, to be exact.
And now, the silliest question of all. Buckle up!

short.title: How Long to Drive to the Sun?

lines.say: What if you could drive a car all the way to the Sun?
Road trip! Are we there yet?
Let's do the math! The Sun is about one hundred and fifty million kilometers away.
If you drive one hundred kilometers per hour, without stopping, you would arrive after about one hundred and seventy one years!
One hundred and seventy one years?! That's crazy! I'd need so many snacks!
Your great, great, great grandkids would be the ones who arrive!
And when they arrive, the Sun is way too hot to park. Bad plan.
Bonus fact! What if you walked there instead, at five kilometers per hour?
That would take more than three thousand four hundred years! You'd need a LOT of shoes.
Can we take a rocket instead?
Rockets are way faster than cars. But even rockets need months to reach other planets!
Months? I've been floating around for ages. Amateurs.
So for now, we explore the Sun with telescopes and spacecraft. Much faster, and much safer!
And sunlight makes the same trip in just eight minutes. Light is the champion!
Quiz time! About how far away is the Sun? One thousand kilometers, one million kilometers, or one hundred and fifty million kilometers?

show.q: How far away is the Sun?

lines.say: One hundred and fifty million kilometers! Really, really far.
Speed round! Five quick facts. Ready? Go!
One! The Sun has about twenty seven million times more mass than the Moon.
Two! But the Sun is about three hundred and ninety times farther away from us.
Three! Earth's axis is tilted about twenty three point four degrees.
Four! One year on Earth is three hundred sixty five and a quarter days.
Five! Light zooms at more than one billion kilometers per hour.
Whoa. My brain needs a nap now!
That's four wild what ifs! Which one surprised you the most?
Think about it! Moon gone, Earth stopped, Sun off, or the road trip?
The road trip. Obviously. I love snacks.
Here's a challenge. Tell a friend one fact you learned today. That's what real space cadets do!
Tomorrow: four space mysteries nobody can solve!
Subscribe and join the crew. See you tomorrow, space cadets!
